title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 130
paragraphs: And from that came the proverb. Then Cleisthenes called for silence and said to the company: “Gentlemen, suitors of my daughter, I commend you all, and if it were possible I would gratify you all — choosing none of you above the rest and rejecting none. But since that cannot be, as I am deliberating about one girl only, I cannot please all of you. Therefore, to those of you who are passed over in this marriage I give a talent of silver apiece, for the honor you paid me in wishing to marry from my household and for your time spent away from home. And to Megacles son of Alcmaeon, I offer my daughter Agariste in betrothal according to the customs of the Athenians.” Megacles accepted the betrothal, and the marriage was settled by Cleisthenes.
